source_text: Dehinc manus imponitur, per benedictionem advocans et invitans Spiritum sanctum. Sane humano ingenio licebit spiritum in aquam arcessere et concorporationem eorum, accommodatis desuper manibus, alio spiritu tantae claritatis animare; Deo autem in suo organo non licebit per manus sanctas sublimitatem modulari spiritalem? Sed est hoc quoque de veteri sacramento, quo nepotes suos ex Joseph Ephraim et Manassem Jacob, capitibus impositis et intermutatis manibus, benedixerit, et quidem ita transversim obliquatis in se, ut Christum deformantes, jam tunc portenderent benedictionem in Christum futuram. Tunc ille sanctissimus Spiritus super emundata et benedicta corpora libens a Patre descendit, super Baptismi aquas, tanquam pristinam sedem recognoscens, conquiescit, columbae figura delapsus in Dominum, ut natura Spiritus sancti declararetur per animal simplicitatis et innocentiae, quod etiam corporaliter ipso felle careat columba. Ideoque: Estote, inquit, simplices sicut columbae, ne hoc quidem sine argumento praecedentis figurae. Quemadmodum enim post aquas diluvii, quibus iniquitas antiqua purgata est, post Baptismum (ut ita dixerim) mundi pacem coelestis irae praeco columba terris adnuntiavit dimissa ex arca, et cum olea reversa; quod signum etiam apud nationes paci praetenditur: eadem dispositione spiritalis effectus terrae, id est carni nostrae emergenti de lavacro post vetera delicta, columba sancti Spiritus advolat, pacem Dei afferens, emissa de coelis, ubi Ecclesia est arca figurata. Sed mundus rursus delinquit, quo male comparetur Baptismus diluvio. Itaque igni destinatur, sicut et homo qui post Baptismum delicta restaurat, ut hoc quoque in signum admonitionis nostrae debeat accipi.
pass_a_gloss: Then the hand is placed, through blessing calling and inviting Holy Spirit. Indeed to human ingenuity it will be permitted to summon spirit into water and their incorporation, with hands accommodated from above, to animate with another spirit of such great clarity; but to God in His own instrument it will not be permitted through holy hands to modulate spiritual sublimity? But this also is from the old sacrament, by which Jacob blessed his grandchildren from Joseph, Ephraim and Manasseh, with hands imposed on their heads and interchangeably, and indeed in such a way crosswise and obliquely in themselves, that deforming Christ, they then already portended the future blessing in Christ. Then that most holy Spirit willingly descends from Father over purified and blessed bodies, over Baptism waters, as if recognizing former seat, rests, having fallen in the form of a dove into Lord, so that the nature of Holy Spirit might be declared through an animal of simplicity and innocence, which dove also corporally lacks bile. And therefore: Be, He says, simple as doves, not even this without precedent figure. For just as after flood waters, by which old iniquity was purified, after Baptism (so to speak) dove announced to earth the peace of heavenly wrath, dismissed from ark, and with olive branch returned; which sign is also held out to nations for peace: by the same disposition spiritual effect to earth, that is to our flesh emerging from washing after former sins, Holy Spirit dove flies, bringing peace of God, sent from heavens, where Church is figured ark. But world again sins, by which Baptism is compared unfavorably to flood. And so it is destined for fire, just as also man who after Baptism restores sins, so that this also ought to be taken as a sign of our admonition.

bible_refs.note: Jacob blessed his grandchildren from Joseph, Ephraim and Manasseh

pass_b_english: Then the hand is placed, through blessing calling and inviting the Holy Spirit. Indeed, human ingenuity permits summoning a spirit into the water and animating their incorporation with another spirit of such great clarity, by placing hands from above; but will God not be permitted, in His own instrument, to modulate spiritual sublimity through holy hands? This, too, belongs to the old sacrament by which Jacob blessed his grandchildren from Joseph, Ephraim and Manasseh, with hands imposed on their heads and crossed—in such a way that, by deforming Christ, they then already portended the future blessing in Christ (Genesis 48:14). Then that most holy Spirit descends willingly from the Father upon purified and blessed bodies, upon the waters of Baptism, as if recognizing a former seat; He rests, having fallen in the form of a dove upon the Lord, so that the nature of the Holy Spirit might be declared through an animal of simplicity and innocence, which also corporally lacks bile. And therefore: 'Be simple as doves,' He says—not even this without a precedent figure. For just as after the flood waters, by which ancient iniquity was purged, after Baptism (so to speak) the dove announced to the earth the peace of heavenly wrath, dismissed from the ark and returning with an olive branch—which sign is also held out to nations for peace—by the same disposition the dove of the Holy Spirit flies to the spiritual effect upon the earth, that is, our flesh emerging from the washing after former sins, bringing the peace of God, sent from the heavens where the Church is figured as the ark. But the world sins again, by which Baptism is compared unfavorably to the flood. And so it is destined for fire, just as the man who after Baptism restores sins, so that this also ought to be taken as a sign of our admonition.

review.notes: The translation accurately captures the Latin text. Pass A and Pass B are consistent with the source. The addition of (Genesis 48:14) in Pass B is a correct identification of the allusion to Jacob blessing Ephraim and Manasseh. The translation of 'intermutatis manibus' as 'crossed' in Pass B and 'interchangeably' in Pass A are both acceptable interpretations of the Latin describing the crossing of hands. All clauses, including the complex comparison between the dove/flood and the Spirit/Baptism, are preserved.
